newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: French, German royal jewels on sale next week.
newsitem.headline: French, German royal jewels on sale next week.

text.p: Part of the French crown jewels, including a mid-19th century tiara set with sapphires, diamonds and pearls, could fetch $1 million at auction next week, Sotheby's said on Friday.
In the latest sign of tough times for European royalty, it has been put on the market by the current owners, the Comte and Comtesse de Paris, head of the royal house of Orleans.

The stunning regal suite -- comprising the tiara, matching earrings, brooches, corsage ornament and centre plaque of a bracelet -- belonged to Queen Marie-Amelie of France (1782-1866), wife of King Louis-Philippe d'Orleans.

Some 30 historic pieces from another former European royal collection, being sold off by the heir of the German Imperial and Royal Prussian House, are estimated to go for $300,000 at Wednesday's spring auction in Geneva.
They belonged to Princess Kira of Prussia, Grand Duchess of Russia, great grand-daughter of both Queen Victoria and Tsar Alexander II of Russia and wife of Prince Louis Ferdinand of Prussia.
"It is unusual to have items from two royal collections -- the French crown jewels and the Kaiser's family," said David Bennett, director of Sotheby's jewellery department.
"It is extremely rare to have jewels coming to sale directly from the family," he told reporters.

Prince Louis Ferdinand died three years ago. His grandson, Prince Georg Friedrich von Preussen, says in the auction catalogue that, as heir, he decided that the jewels and 36 silver table pieces "should be sold in order to help with the restructuring of the family's holdings".
"My grandfather, having been the grandson of Emperor Wilhelm II, lived in quite a different style to the family today and it became clear that some of his effects would no longer be needed," he said.
"In view of today's growing interest in German history, I believe it is the right moment to offer these objects for sale."
But the highlight of Wednesday's sale at Sotheby's will be the jewels of Queen Marie-Amelie.
"I don't know who will buy it, although there is interest in the Far East," Bennett said. "It is certainly a rare museum piece."
